body:
Proposal from mkinney (2026-11-18): "Should we formalize our QA swarm in an issue ... so all can track what it is doing? ... It is starting to feel like integration tests."

What exists: since 2026-11-17 mkinney's agents design parts in the latest SolidCraft and make them in the latest CamCraft end to end (design -> project -> operations -> generate -> verify -> post), and write a report per part. Ten parts so far (p01-p10: flange, bracket, stepped block, threaded boss, wrapped cylinder, all-ops mill part, lathe shaft, microARC 4 part, turning on a mill, plasma plate). They found about 100 problems; filed so far: #2437, #2440, #2443, #2578, #2579, #2580.

## Proposal: two layers

1. **Deterministic (in the normal gate, no AI):** every QA part that posts becomes an example-catalog case (#2392, `cargo xtask catalog`): the `.sc`/`.step`, a recorded build script (the MCP/CamScript steps) and the byte-pinned `.nc`. A regression then shows in the normal gate at no AI cost.
2. **Exploratory (agents, on contributors' own machines, NOT in GitHub Actions):** the agents need AI subscriptions and keys, and AGENTS.md keeps secrets off the self-hosted runners. Runs are made visible by:
   - one pinned tracking issue with a comment per run (versions, parts, results, issues filed);
   - the part briefs in the repository (for example `qa/briefs/`), so anyone can read and improve them;
   - a `source:qa` label on every issue a run files.

## When to run

- after each minor cut tag (test what users download);
- after each SolidCraft release, at most daily (the `.sc` import, #2578, broke this way);
- on demand.

## Decisions for the maintainer

- Do passing parts go into the catalog (#2392) as cases, and is the repository the right home for the briefs?
- The `source:qa` label.
